subject: Custom uptime tolerance & order-form language for MedTerra — draft redlines
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medterrahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medterrahealth.com
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom uptime tolerance and order-form language (MSA/SOW attachments)

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Quick context: we're finalizing the vendor packet for our API-backed inference platform and need firm language in the order form and SOW that reflects our operational requirements. Two asks:

1) Uptime tolerance: we're aiming to contract a 99.7% monthly uptime commitment for the dedicated deployment used by our production routing (this is higher than your standard 99.5% for Dedicated). We understand this may fall under an exception/addendum. Please confirm what carve-outs you need (maintenance windows, force majeure, planned upgrades) and whether you can provide a tailored SLA addendum.

2) Latency SLO: for inference p95 (inference completion for request type: chat/streaming), we need a p95 <= 250ms for short-text interactive calls (<=128 tokens). If you cannot commit to that number globally, we'd like fallback language that specifies regional routing and an order form exhibit that details target regions and fallback model/instance classes.

Can you send a redline of (a) MSA exhibit, (b) SOW appendix that lists rollout regions and fallback behavior, and (c) the order form line items (the precise SLA wording + credit calculation formula you would accept)? If you prefer, we can accept an exception addendum and incorporate it into the order form.

Attaching our internal doc (procurement asked me to attach) but we expect your legal and product ops to propose wording. We need this back (ideally) in 48 hours for procurement review.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Kim
Director, Platform Ops — MedTerra Health
---
Attachments: MedTerra_uptime_requirements_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medterrahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom uptime tolerance and order-form language (MSA/SOW attachments)

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the doc.

We're happy to run this as a formal SLA exception/addendum. Quick notes:
- We can evaluate 99.7% monthly uptime for a Dedicated pool, but we will need to define explicit maintenance windows and a clear list of excluded events (e.g., scheduled kernel upgrades, hypervisor patches, third-party cloud provider outages).
- For the latency SLO, p95 <= 250ms at <=128 tokens is aggressive for multi-tenant shared fleets; for Dedicated we can target this in the primary region if the pool spec uses A100-class (or equivalent) instances and a pinned model variant. We will propose fallback/route policies in the order form exhibit.

I have looped Ben (sales lead) and Laura (legal program manager) — Ben, can you draft the order-form insert and credit formula? Laura, can your team prepare an MSA exhibit and SOW appendix that capture: the exact maintenance carve-outs, monitoring/measurement methodology (how p95 is calculated), and the mitigation/credit application?

Alex — timeline: Ben and I can get redlines to you by end of day Tuesday (48 hours). If procurement needs an internal review faster, let us know which clauses are highest priority.

Best,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Director | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medterrahealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom uptime tolerance and order-form language (MSA/SOW attachments)

Alex / Soojin / Laura — attaching a first-pass redline set. Highlights below and included in the redline doc:

- Order form SLA line (proposed): "Redwood will provide Monthly Uptime of 99.7% for the Dedicated Capacity specified in the Order Form, except for Excluded Downtime. Excluded Downtime includes scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice, customer-initiated configuration changes, and force majeure events."

- Credit calculation (proposed exhibit snippet): "If Monthly Uptime falls below 99.7%, credits are applied as a percentage of monthly Dedicated fees: 99.0–99.7% = 10% credit; 98.0–98.99% = 25% credit; <98.0% = 50% credit. Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for unavailability under this SLA for Dedicated Capacity."

- Latency SLO exhibit: we propose region-scoped p95 targets that are only applicable when the customer purchases the 'low-latency regional guarantee' add-on. If purchased: p95 <= 250ms for <=128 tokens measured at our ingress point for the customer's dedicated pool in the specified region. If the add-on is not purchased, latency language will be advisory and routing/fallback behavior will be documented in the SOW appendix.

- Fallback behavior: the SOW appendix will list primary region, failover region(s), and permitted model variants (e.g., quantized variants) for failover. Also includes a 'graceful degradation' policy to preserve availability for critical traffic.

I'm attaching three files: MedTerra_MSA_redline_v1.pdf, MedTerra_SOW_attachment.docx, orderform_uptime_redline.docx. I also created a DocuSign envelope for a narrow addendum (link below) if you want to expedite signature on the exception addendum after legal signs off.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/medterra/MT-2027-042
Drive (redlines): https://drive.redwood.com/shared/MedTerra/uptime-playbook-v1

Please review and call out any clauses you want softened. Laura — can you confirm the MSA exhibit references our monitoring method (ingress point measurement, p95 computed over 5-minute rolling windows aggregated daily) and the credit window?

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: MedTerra_MSA_redline_v1.pdf, MedTerra_SOW_attachment.docx, orderform_uptime_redline.docx
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@medterrahealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@medterrahealth.com
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: custom uptime tolerance and order-form language (MSA/SOW attachments)

Thanks — received the redlines and the DocuSign link. A couple quick clarifying questions before our procurement team starts internal routing:

1) The credit bands look reasonable. Can you confirm whether credits are pro-rated by impacted routes or only applied at the account/month level? Our internal billing wants route-level visibility because we run both critical and non-critical flows on the same Dedicated pool.

2) For the latency add-on: if we purchase the low-latency regional guarantee, is there an SLA penalty if the deviation is due to customer-generated burst above the provisioned qps for that pool? We'd prefer that customer-generated overloads (clear traffic spikes) be excluded from credit calculations.

3) Timeline: procurement will do a legal and security review once we have the final redlines. If we sign the addendum, we'd like a committed rollout plan (dates + region) in the SOW appendix. Is EOD Friday realistic for the final redline set?

If you can answer those 3 points in your next update, we can queue the package to legal.

Best,
Alex
